Stated Claim / Post Context:
Report: Trump May Hold off on Renewed Iran Strikes Unless Tehran Provokes U.S.

President Donald Trump has told senior advisers he may hold off on renewed military strikes against Iran unless Tehran or its Houthi allies in Yemen engage in further provocations, according to a report Saturday.
The post Report: Trump May Hold off on Renewed Iran Strikes Unless Tehran Provokes U.S. appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
President Donald Trump has told senior advisers he may hold off on renewed military strikes against Iran unless Tehran or its Houthi allies in Yemen engage in further provocations, according to a report Saturday.

Trump raised the possibility during recent discussions with senior national security advisers and after receiving intelligence briefings, Reuters reported, citing three people familiar with the deliberations. The president has not made a final decision on whether to resume military operations against the Islamic Republic.

The discussions come amid appeals from Middle Eastern allies to avoid another major escalation, even as Israel continues pressing Washington to launch additional strikes against the Iranian regime.

According to the report, Trump sought the views of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan during separate telephone conversations in recent weeks. Both leaders urged him to avoid renewed attacks, although neither secured a commitment from the president.

During an October 31 conversation, Trump reportedly told the Saudi crown prince that he intended to strike Iran following the midterm elections. Bin Salman urged restraint, arguing that the administration’s economic sanctions were already weakening Tehran.

The president also held three conversations with Erdogan beginning in late October, according to the Turkish presidency, which said their discussion last Saturday focused on efforts to ease tensions between Washington and Tehran.

Trump publicly acknowledged the appeals Thursday, explaining that several regional allies had asked him to avoid an immediate escalation.

“I could end it immediately, but at the request of the nations that I am looking to protect, we are doing it a little bit longer way, a bit more civilly,” Trump told broadcaster Stephen A. Smith.

The president identified Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, and Bahrain among the countries seeking restraint amid concerns that renewed American strikes could trigger Iranian retaliation across the Gulf.

The appeals coincide with American intelligence assessments indicating that the U.S. naval blockade and economic sanctions are severely damaging Iran’s economy, strengthening Washington’s ability to maintain pressure without immediately resuming major military operations.
